claims.text: The initial FCC/B2 eutectic HEA has a fine lamellar or cellular microstructure with nanoscale ordered B2 precipitates in an FCC matrix.
Intermediate aging at approximately 400–600 °C evolves local chemical order and coarsens B2 domains.
The proposed aging duration permits LCO evolution and B2 coarsening without grain coarsening or impurity segregation.
LCO-ordering kinetics are maximized within an intermediate-temperature window in which B2 remains thermodynamically stable.
Aging produces a continuous, percolating network of ordered B2 domains at FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
Increased LCO at FCC/B2 boundaries increases lattice friction for partial-dislocation motion.
Chemical ordering and lattice-parameter mismatch at evolving B2/FCC interfaces create a rough energy landscape.
The rough energy landscape equalizes defect mobilities at the B2/FCC interfaces.
The ordered interfacial network pins partial dislocations and raises the critical stress for cross-slip and dislocation multiplication.
Suppression of dislocation bypass, cross-slip, and multiplication causes brittle fracture and a transient loss of ductility.
At higher aging temperatures, thermal energy overcomes the frictional barrier or the ordered network breaks into isolated islands, restoring ductility.
Ductility varies non-monotonically with aging, dropping sharply to near-zero elongation and then recovering at higher temperatures or longer times.
The as-cast baseline contains fine, non-percolating B2 precipitates and has lower interfacial LCO.
The as-cast fine FCC/B2 composite exhibits high ductility and strong work hardening because hard B2 regions pin dislocations moving through soft FCC regions.
Embrittlement occurs only after B2 domains form a continuous path and before coarsening or thermal disorder makes that path ineffective or isolated.
The embrittlement temperature window and critical percolation fraction depend on alloy composition, including Al content.
In CoNiCrFeMn HEA nanowires, lattice-parameter differences create friction that hinders partial-dislocation motion, hardens the material, and lowers ductility.
The nanowire friction mechanism can be scaled to ordered phase boundaries in bulk FCC/B2 eutectic HEAs.
A continuous ordered network reaching a critical volume fraction causes immediate failure.
Rapid quenching after aging can produce a chemically disordered B2 control while isolating ordering from coarsening.

contradictions.description: Network percolation is described both as the event that initiates immediate failure and as a threshold that coarsening can pass to restore ductility. The text does not define how further coarsening converts a percolating network into isolated islands.

Recovery is partly attributed to greater thermal activation at a higher aging temperature, while mechanical testing may occur after cooling to room temperature. Thermal activation during aging cannot directly overcome dislocation friction during a later room-temperature test unless an irreversible structural change is specified.
